title: Category: Aging and Elder Care | Institute for Family Studies
gist: This is an Institute for Family Studies blog category index for Aging and Elder Care, listing article titles only (AI safeguards for seniors, loneliness and childlessness, multigenerational living, homeless seniors) with no substantive body text.

insights.claim: The Institute for Family Studies' most recent Aging and Elder Care piece (September 17, 2026) is Jared Hayden's 'Older Americans Need AI Safeguards, Too', marking AI risks to seniors as a current focus.
insights.speaker: Institute for Family Studies
insights.so_what: Family-policy think tanks are adding seniors to their AI-safety agenda, a broadening of the tech-regulation coalition.
insights.locator: Older Americans Need AI Safeguards, Too

insights.claim: IFS links elder-care problems to family structure, with titles connecting loneliness to childlessness (Rosemary L. Hopcroft, March 2026) and smaller families to homeless seniors (Stephen Eide, 2024).
insights.speaker: Institute for Family Studies
insights.so_what: Low fertility is framed as a future elder-care and senior-housing liability, relevant to long-run care-demand and public spending assumptions.
insights.locator: 'All the Lonely People': Loneliness Is Exacerbated

insights.claim: Multigenerational living and adult children's co-residence with aging parents recur as proposed elder-care solutions in IFS coverage.
insights.speaker: Institute for Family Studies
insights.so_what: Multigenerational housing is a recurring theme; watch for housing and policy demand around co-residence.
insights.locator: Multigenerational Living: Is It a Solution
